item.title: Uniformly Bounded Orthonormal Bases of Homogeneous Polynomials on the Complex Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.14160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We resolve the long-standing problem of Rudin concerning uniformly bounded orthonormal bases of homogeneous polynomials on complex unit spheres. Specifically, we show that for every $K \geq 2$ and $N \geq 0$ there exists a basis of degree $N$ homogeneous polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^K$ that is orthonormal with respect to the surface measure of the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^K$ and uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on $K$ on the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^K$. Bourgain resolved the case $K = 2$ in 1985 and the case $K = 3$ in 2016. No cases $K \geq 4$ were previously known.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Gon\c{c}alves, Jo\~ao P. Ferreira, Maksym Radziwi\l{}\l{}

item.title: A series with a Cantorval set of subsums and ratio of consecutive terms tending to $1/2$ (the second Jones problem)
item.description: arXiv:2610.14251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The second Jones problem (2011) consists in determining whether there exists a convergent positive series for which the ratio of consecutive terms has a limit and the set of subsums is a Cantorval; in the survey by G{\l}{\k a}b and Prus-Wi\'sniowski (2026) this problem is included in the list of open problems. In this paper, a family of such series is constructed explicitly as combinations of blocks of the form $\frac{2^k-1}{2^t} + \frac{2^{k-1}}{2^t} + \frac{2^{k-2}}{2^t} + \cdots + \frac{2}{2^t}$, where $t$ is the index of the last term of the block in the series and $k\ge2$ is the length of the block. For each series of the family it is proved that its set of subsums contains an interval and is not a finite union of closed intervals, and hence is a Cantorval. The proof relies on mixed-radix numerical systems with a redundant alphabet and uses an idea of Guthrie and Nymann (1988). If the lengths of the blocks tend to infinity, then the limit of the ratio of consecutive terms of such series is $\tfrac{1}{2}$, which, by a result of Jones, is the only possible value of the limit for which the set of subsums of a series can be a Cantorval. Thus, an affirmative answer to the second Jones problem is obtained.
item.dc:creator: Mykola Pratsiovytyi, Yaroslav Vynnyshyn, Oleh Vynnyshyn

item.title: Parametric Families of Minimal Positive Cubature Formulas of Degrees 4 and 6 on the 2-Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.14287v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study minimal positive cubature formulas on the two-dimensional sphere of degrees four and six, with ten and eighteen nodes, respectively. We prove the regularity of Popov's symmetric formulas and establish that their local families of deformations are two-dimensional, up to rotations. We obtain algebraic relations between the weights and pairwise inner products of the nodes. For degree four, we construct a one-parameter family with half-turn symmetry connecting the formulas of Popov and Heo--Xu. We also give a self-contained proof that eighteen nodes are minimal for degree six.
item.dc:creator: D. V. Gorbachev

item.title: On best approximation and estimates of Bohr--Favard type on the sphere for functions with bounded Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2610.14811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the best constants in estimates of the $L^\infty$ norm of functions on the sphere with bounded Laplacian whose first spherical harmonic components vanish. In every dimension $d\geq2$, these constants are expressed through weighted $L^1$ extremal polynomials. On $S^2$ the constant is an explicit positive series, and the best coefficient of $n^{-2}$ is $7\zeta(3)/4$. On $S^3$ the best coefficient of $n^{-2}$ is a positive integral involving the H\"ormander--Bernhardsson extremal function. In higher dimensions the rescaled extremal polynomials converge to weighted entire extremals, which give asymptotic formulas for the Bohr constants on $S^4$ and $S^6$. The most unexpected and, in our view, interesting observation is that, for every fixed $n\geq2$ on $S^2$ and $S^3$, the constants in best approximation estimates are \emph{strictly smaller} than the corresponding Bohr--Favard constants.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Solyanik

item.title: Oscillatory Integral Operators Along the Paraboloid and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.14841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove decay estimates for oscillatory integral operators along $(y_1, y_2, y_1^2+y_2^2)$ in the finite field and the continuous settings. In the continuous setting, our result allows a bi-parameter maximal modulation, which extends the one-parameter version previously established by Pierce and Yung. Our approach is different from theirs. Then we discuss three applications of our estimates: a power saving bound for certain pattern finding problem in finite fields, a short approach to $L^p$ boundedness of an one-parameter Pierce--Yung operator, and $L^p$ boundedness of a bi-parameter Pierce--Yung operator.
item.dc:creator: Jianghao Zhang

item.title: There are no unconditional Schauder frames of exponentials in $L^p$ spaces, $p \ne 2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.14842v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We proved recently that there are no unconditional Schauder frames of exponentials in the space $L^p(\Omega)$, $1 \le p < 2$, for any set $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ of finite measure. For $p > 2$, we proved that the same holds provided that $\Omega$ has nonempty interior, but the general case remained open. In this note we close this gap, i.e., we establish that exponentials cannot form an unconditional Schauder frame in $L^p(\Omega)$, $p \ne 2$, without any additional assumptions on the set $\Omega$ of finite measure other than measurability.
item.dc:creator: Nir Lev, Anton Tselishchev

item.title: Description Complexity Bounds for Analytic Approximations of Lipschitz Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.14893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how many bits are needed to write down an elementary analytic expression that uniformly approximates a Lipschitz function. Expressions are finite trees over the basis $\{+,-,\times,\div,\exp\}$ with the variables and rational constants, and their size is $\dc(f)$, the length of the shortest description of $f$ in a fixed binary description language. For functions of one variable we prove that every $L$-Lipschitz $F:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ has an everywhere-defined approximant of accuracy $\Delta$ with $\dc(f)\le C\,(L/\Delta+\lg(1/\Delta+2))$ for all $L,\Delta>0$, by a linear spline smoothed with logistic ramps in a description language with one repetition construct. We prove a matching lower bound valid for \emph{every} description language: for $\Delta\le 1/36$ and every $L>0$ some $L$-Lipschitz function needs at least $\tfrac1{16}(L/\Delta+\lg(1/\Delta+2))$ bits. Hence the worst-case description complexity is $\Theta(L/\Delta+\lg(1/\Delta+2))$. For functions on $[0,1]^d$ the same method gives $\Theta_d\bigl((L/\Delta)^d+\lg(1/\Delta+2)\bigr)$, using a tensor-product spline whose coefficients are mixed second differences and cost $O(d)$ bits each. Without the repetition construct the upper bounds carry an additional logarithmic factor, whose necessity for plain expression trees is left open. A reference encoder, decoder and evaluator confirm the constructions numerically, and figures and tables report the checks.
item.dc:creator: Artem Vozmishchev

item.title: Multiple non-collision periodic solutions for second order singular differential systems with parameters
item.description: arXiv:2610.14910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, new existence and multiplicity results for positive periodic solutions of singular second-order problems under sublinear and superlinear growth assumptions at infinity are established. Two aspects of our results should be highlighted in comparison with the existing literature. On the one hand, they allow for the consideration of systems exhibiting mixed behavior: sublinear in one component and superlinear in another. On the other hand, in the superlinear case, the existence of up to four positive solutions is established, whereas only two were obtained in previous works. Our approach is based on a recently established vectorial version of the Krasnoselskii-Guo fixed point theorem in product spaces.
item.dc:creator: Laura Mar\'ia Fern\'andez-Pardo, Jorge Rodr\'iguez-L\'opez

item.title: A proof of Kahane's conjecture in the Wiener algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.14981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Kahane's conjecture: if a continuous unimodular function $F$ on the circle satisfies $\|F^n\|_{A(\mathbb{T})}=o(\log|n|)$ as $|n|\to\infty$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, then $F(x)=e^{i(mx+b)}$ for some $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ and $b\in\mathbb{R}$. The main step is a logarithmic lower bound for averages: for every nonconstant real-valued $\varphi\in A(\mathbb{T})$, $\frac{1}{T}\int_a^{a+T}\|e^{it\varphi}\|_{A(\mathbb{T})}dt \ge c_\varphi\log T \quad(a\in\mathbb{R},\ T\ge T_\varphi)$, where $c_\varphi>0$ and $T_\varphi>1$ are independent of $a$. The proof uses exact sampling on finite subgroups of the circle, uniformly bounded localized modulations, and the weighted non-harmonic Littlewood inequality of Jaming--Kellay--Saba. A suitable cutoff and a small linear perturbation of the phase ensure that a fixed positive proportion of the coefficients at the beginning of the frequency ordering have modulus one. Passing to integer powers and removing the degree of the circle map yield Kahane's conjecture without any additional smoothness assumptions. We also give equivalent phase, convolution, and operator formulations, and derive consequences for homomorphisms of weighted Wiener algebras and for higher-dimensional tori.
item.dc:creator: Przemys{\l}aw Ohrysko

item.title: Compactness and essential norms for two-weight fractional Riesz transforms on curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.15002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a compact two-weight $T1$ theorem for the $\alpha$-fractional Riesz vector, $0\leq\alpha<n$, when one measure is supported on a compact regular $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ curve $\Gamma$. The measures may have common point masses. Under the global boundedness assumptions, we give a two-sided estimate for the essential norm in terms of Muckenhoupt and testing constants computed after restricting both measures to small cubes. Compactness is equivalent to the uniform vanishing of these local bounds as the cube side length tends to zero. The smooth truncations have a unique weak operator limit and converge in operator norm in the compact case. For arclength measure and distance power weights, we determine the compactness ranges for Green gradients on bounded tubes and for Newtonian gradients and Biot--Savart fields on the whole space. The whole-space operators in these ranges are compact but are not Hilbert--Schmidt. When $\alpha=n-1$ and both measures have positive continuous arclength densities $a,b$ on the same closed curve, we obtain the exact essential norm $\pi c_{n-1,n}\max_\Gamma\sqrt{ab}$.
item.dc:creator: Ji Li, Chun-Yen Shen, Chaojie Wen, Brett D. Wick, Liangchuan Wu

item.title: Weighted norm inequalities for operators with new Muckenhoupt type weights in the Bessel setting and applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.15260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\lambda>-1/2,\neq0$. Consider the Bessel operators \begin{align*} \Delta_\lambda:=-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}-\frac{2\lambda}{x}\frac{d}{dx} \end{align*} on $\mathbb{R}_+$. In this paper, we first establish several characterizations for $\widetilde{A}_{\infty,\lambda}$ weights introduced by Li et al. (Math. Z. 309(1) (2025), Paper No. 13, 29pp), which are different from the previous $A_p$ class with respect to the measure $x^{2\lambda}dx$. Among these characterizations, we obtain the sharp reverse H\"{o}lder inequality (RHI) for $\widetilde{A}_{\infty,\lambda}$ weights. As applications of RHI, we derive a precise open property of $\widetilde{A}_{p,\lambda}$ weights, and obtain a sharp weighted bounds for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator $\mathcal{M}_\lambda$ associated to $\Delta_\lambda$, which was missing in the previous papers. Next, we also establish several extrapolation theorems related to $\widetilde{A}_{p,\lambda}$ weights. Furthermore, we characterize the restricted weighted weak type estimates for $\mathcal{M}_\lambda$ via a new class of weights $\widetilde{A}_{p,\lambda}^{\mathcal{R}}$, which is strictly larger than $\widetilde{A}_{p,\lambda}$. Meanwhile, we obtain quantitative restricted weighted weak type $(p,p)$ bounds for sparse operators. As applications, we derive various kinds of weighted inequalities for Riesz transforms, maximal operators, square functions, variation operators and their commutators associated to $\Delta_\lambda$.
item.dc:creator: Yongming Wen, Huoxiong Wu

item.title: Discrete intermediate dimensions: endpoints, spectra and quasi-isometric invariance
item.description: arXiv:2610.15410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce upper and lower discrete intermediate dimensions for unbounded subsets of Euclidean space and extend them to metric spaces. The definitions restrict the covering radii within a scale-dependent range of dyadic shells and take a supremum over an auxiliary parameter. The resulting dimensions are monotone in the parameter and recover the Barlow--Taylor discrete Hausdorff dimension at zero. We prove continuity at every positive parameter, with a sharp quantitative bound, and give an example with a jump at zero. At the upper endpoint, the upper dimension equals upper mass dimension for uniformly discrete Euclidean sets; the analogous lower mass identity fails. We establish a mass distribution principle and prove quasi-isometric invariance under a uniform coarse packing condition. For spaces with uniform polynomial volume growth, we construct clustered subsets attaining the continuity bound. Independent thinning truncates these spectra at the resulting mass dimension, almost surely for all parameters simultaneously. Applications include the discrete Heisenberg group with its word metric and the ranges of simple symmetric random walks.
item.dc:creator: Jinjun Li, Lifeng Xi, Shuqin Zhang

item.title: Weak type (1,1) bound criterion for maximal truncated singular integral operators with rough kernels
item.description: arXiv:2610.15820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proves the weak type (1,1) boundedness for maximal truncated singular integral operators with rough non-convolution kernels of the form $\Omega(x-y) K(x,y)$, where $\Omega$ is homogeneous of degree zero with $\Omega \in L\log L(\sS^{d-1})$ and $K$ is a standard Calder\'on-Zygmund kernel. This extends the recent resolution of the classical convolution case by Lai \cite{Lai2025weak} to a wider class of operators.
item.dc:creator: Xudong Lai, Lingxin Xu

item.title: A Sharp Lower Bound for Integral Menger Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.15981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that round circles $C_L$ are the unique minimisers of integral Menger curvature among embedded closed $C^1$ curves $\gamma$ of prescribed length $L$ for every $p\geq 2$, i.e. $M_p(C_L) \leq M_p(\gamma)$, with equality if and only if $\gamma$ parametrises a round circle. The proof combines a three-point symmetrisation, an analysis of diagonal truncations, and the periodic Wirtinger inequality. For $p>3$, known self-avoidance and regularity results extend the minimisation result to closed rectifiable curves without assuming embeddedness or smoothness, provided the length of the curve image equals $L$. In particular, $M_p$ detects the unknot and is basic for $p>3$, thereby answering a question posed repeatedly in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Scholtes

item.title: Multi-scale analysis for multilinear operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.16088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a unified multi-scale framework for sparse domination of multilinear operators beyond the multilinear Calder\'{o}n--Zygmund theory. More precisely, under mild hypotheses on a support condition, weak type and restricted strong type uniform bounds for finite partial sums, and single-scale improving and regularity estimates, we establish $(r_1, \ldots, r_m, s')$-sparse form bound for a family of localized $m$-linear operators uniformly over all finite partial sums. This sparse bound yields weighted norm inequalities for the corresponding multilinear Muckenhoupt classes $A_{\vec{p}, (\vec{r}, s)}$, including the quasi-Banach range. As applications, we determine the optimal open sparse range for multilinear rough singular integrals, and characterize sparse domination for bilinear pseudo-differential operators. Further applications include sparse bounds for bilinear oscillatory Fourier multipliers, bilinear spherical maximal operators, and bilinear Bochner--Riesz means.
item.dc:creator: Mingming Cao, Binyu Du, K\^{o}z\^{o} Yabuta

item.title: On Mattila's intersection problem in the plane: sharp dimension and positive measure of rotated difference sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.16114v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(A,B\subset\R^2\) be nonempty Borel sets. We prove that \[ \dimH(gA-B)\ge\min\{\dimH A+\dimH B,2\} \] for almost all \(g\in\mathrm O(2)\). This bound is sharp in general, and the proof gives a corresponding statement for the lower Hausdorff dimension of convolutions of Frostman measures. We also prove that \(\LL^2(gA-B)>0\) for almost all \(g\) if both dimensions exceed \((\sqrt{13}-1)/2\). The second result follows from an angular decomposition, refined decoupling and a two-ends Furstenberg estimate. Some applications on intersection patterns are also addressed.
item.dc:creator: Thang Pham, Chun-Yen Shen, Dung The Tran

item.title: Two-weight T1 theorem for fractional Riesz transforms: one measure supported on a $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ curve
item.description: arXiv:2610.16123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $0\leq\alpha<n$, and let $\sigma$ and $\omega$ be locally finite positive Borel measures on $\R^n$, possibly with common point masses. Suppose that one measure is supported on a compact regular $C^{1,\mathrm{Dini}}$ curve. We prove that the $\alpha$-fractional Riesz vector maps $L^2(\sigma)$ to $L^2(\omega)$ if and only if the two $\cA_2^\alpha$ conditions with holes, the two punctured $A_2^\alpha$ conditions, and the forward and dual testing conditions over rotated cubes hold. The theorem includes curves whose tangent is not H\"older continuous of any positive order. Straightening such a curve produces a kernel whose first derivatives need not satisfy the H\"older estimates required by the energy-side-condition $T1$ theorem. We prove both strong energy conditions in the straightened coordinates using only a sufficiently small graph slope, and show that these conditions are preserved under biLipschitz changes of variables. The Dini condition makes the errors in the kernel and testing comparisons summable. We then transfer the energy conditions back and apply the $T1$ theorem to the original smooth Riesz kernel. We also obtain a two-weight criterion for Green gradients with curve-supported sources. For arclength measure on the curve and observation measure $\dist(x,\Gamma)^\beta\,dx$, the range is $\beta>n-3$ in a bounded tube and $n-3<\beta<n-2$ in $\R^n$. The endpoints fail logarithmically whenever the measure is locally finite. In dimension three, the corresponding whole-space range for the Biot--Savart field with arbitrary vector densities is $0<\beta<1$.
item.dc:creator: Ji Li, Chun-Yen Shen, Eric Sawyer, Brett Wick

item.title: $L^p$-weighted cone restriction estimates
item.description: arXiv:2610.16294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Fourier extension estimates for the truncated cone in $\R^{n+1}$ with weights satisfying an $m$-dimensional ball condition only at radii between $1$ and $R^{1/2}$, where $0<m\le n-1$. Within the discrete induction framework of Du--Li--Wang--Zhang, we obtain a family of bounds by combining multilinear refined Strichartz inequalities, narrow decoupling, and Lorentz rescaling. We also give lightplank, lattice, and hybrid lattice--Knapp examples.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyu Wang

item.title: Translational self-affine tiles in $\mathbb{R}^n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.16340v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two basic problems in the theory of integral self-affine tiles are to characterize the digit sets that generate translational tiles and to understand whether such tiles admit periodic translational tilings. We give a complete solution to the first problem: for an expanding integer matrix $\mathbf{A}$ and a digit set $\mathcal{D}\subset\mathbb{Z}^n$ with $\#\mathcal{D}=|\det\mathbf{A}|$, the self-affine set $T(\mathbf{A},\mathcal{D})$ is a tile if and only if, for some $N\geq1$, the iterated digit set $\mathcal{D}_{{\mathbf{A}},N}$ is of skew-product form with respect to $\mathbf{A}^N$. As a consequence, every integral self-affine tile admits a fully periodic self-replicating $q$-fold tiling. Moreover, $q$ divides $|T(\mathbf{A},\mathcal{D})|$. In dimension two we prove more: every integral self-affine tile admits a fully periodic tiling. In particular, the periodic tiling conjecture holds for integral self-affine tiles in $\mathbb{R}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Li-Xiang An, Ting-Ting He

item.title: Reverse H\"older Class and Two-Parameter Good-$\lambda$ Inequality over Hausdorff Content
item.description: arXiv:2610.16405v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical harmonic analysis is built upon Lebesgue (or more general) measure. Such a framework is remarkably successful for sets of full ambient dimension, but becomes intrinsically insensitive to lower-dimensional geometry: curves, surfaces, and more generally fractal subsets of \(\mathbb R^n\) with zero \(n\)-dimensional Lebesgue measure. In contrast, Hausdorff content provides a dimension-sensitive notion of size for lower-dimensional sets or fractal sets, but harmonic analysis in this setting is still largely limited to maximal operators. In this paper, we establish a weighted two-parameter good-\(\lambda\) inequality under Hausdorff content setting, providing a route toward other general operators from maximal operators over Hausdorff content. To do this, we firstly identify an appropriate reverse H\"older class $\mathcal R\mathcal H_{q,\delta}$ associated with Hausdorff content, and then prove the self-improving property of $\mathcal R\mathcal H_{q,\delta}$ by establishing the fundamental equivalence between reverse H\"older weights and capacitary Muckenhoupt weights. As direct applications, we obtain weighted Fefferman--Stein inequality and some boundedness on general operators over Hausdorff content. The methodology developed in this paper, even when reduced to the Lebesgue measure case, also provide novel insights, which shows that the good-\(\lambda\) principle is not intrinsically tied to an underlying measure, but can extended to a non-additive framework.
item.dc:creator: Long Huang, Yangzhi Zhang, Ciqiang Zhuo

item.title: Schatten--Lorentz properties of commutators with matrix weights
item.description: arXiv:2610.16476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the membership of commutators $[b,T]$ of Calder\'on--Zygmund operators in the Schatten--Lorentz classes in the matrix-weighted setting. Working on a space of homogeneous type $(X,\rho,\mu)$ with a matrix $A_2$ weight $W$, we characterise, for $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $q\in[1,\infty)$, the Schatten--Lorentz norm $\|[b,T]\|_{S^{p,q}(L^2(W))}$ in terms of an oscillation (Besov-type) norm $\|b\|_{\mathrm{Osc}^{p,q}}$ of the symbol: for all $p\in(1,\infty)$, finiteness of $\|b\|_{\mathrm{Osc}^{p,q}}$ is necessary; and for $p>p(\eta)$, where $p(\eta)$ depends on the regularity of the kernel of $T$ and a dimensional parameter of the space, the two-sided estimate $\|[b,T]\|_{S^{p,q}(L^2(W))}\approx\|b\|_{\mathrm{Osc}^{p,q}}$ holds. Extending a recent unified framework for unweighted and scalar-weighted versions of such results by one of us to the matrix-weighted setting, our approach combines the dyadic representation of singular integral operators with the nearly weakly orthogonal (NWO) sequences of Rochberg and Semmes.
item.dc:creator: Tuomas Hyt\"onen, Xingyan Quan

item.title: The manufacture of examples II: the "para-classical" orthogonal polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.16704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Under the stated regularity assumptions, the full orthogonality functionals of the five finite para-families considered here are classical for the respective affine, quadratic, $q$-quadratic, $q$-linear and alternating calculi. For each of the para-Krawtchouk, para-Racah, $q$-para-Racah and $q$-para-Krawtchouk families, two finite solutions of one global structural equation have $N+1$ nodes altogether and common moments through degree $N-1$. Their relative mass changes only the central recurrence coefficients. We prove regularity for every normalised combination with both component masses non-zero and recover the full published functionals and recurrences. The alternating construction identifies para-Bannai-Ito within the same structural framework. For the four non-alternating families, equal positive combinations give persymmetric Jacobi matrices; the known spectral gap criterion then decides perfect state transfer. Explicit parameter correspondences locate the classical components and resonant limits of the full systems. A positive seven-point example shows how further named families can be manufactured without a new governing principle. Counterexamples to mathematical assertions in three of four recent preprints expose the consequences of insufficient hypotheses for finite representations and physical models. In an era of AI-assisted symbolic production, we call for a standard that rewards structural explanation and verification rather than the proliferation of examples.
item.dc:creator: K. Castillo, G. Gordillo-N\'u\~nez

item.title: Asymptotic analysis of the confluent Dotsenko-Fateev system
item.description: arXiv:2610.16970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Dotsenko-Fateev equation is a third-order linear ordinary differential equation studied in two-dimensional conformal field theory. We study the confluent Dotsenko-Fateev system, a rank-three system of linear ordinary differential equations obtained by confluence from a first-order system equivalent to the Dotsenko-Fateev equation. It has an irregular singular point at infinity, and its solutions admit double integral representations of confluent Selberg type. Using these representations, we construct sectorial fundamental solution matrices around infinity, establish their asymptotic expansions, and determine the associated Stokes matrices explicitly. We further study three aspects of the confluent Dotsenko-Fateev system: its equivalence to the degree-two polynomial reduction of the Schr\"{o}dinger equation for the quantum Painlev\'{e} equation of type V, its realization as a restriction of a confluent version of the linear Pfaffian system associated with Appell's hypergeometric function $F_4$, and its reduction to the trivial rank-one equation via integral transforms and a quadratic change of the independent variable.
item.dc:creator: Shunya Adachi

item.title: Finiteness of Fuchsian equations with unitarizable monodromy on compact Riemann surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17116v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, on any compact Riemann surface, there are only finitely many meromorphic projective connections with prescribed singular points and real exponent differences whose projective monodromy is unitarizable. We also establish properness and growth estimates for holonomy, including a relative version for smooth marked families, and derive finiteness results for spherical conical metrics and ramification divisors of stable extensions.
item.dc:creator: Sheng Tan

item.title: Cone restriction via direction-restricted two-ends Furstenberg estimates
item.description: arXiv:2610.17752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a direct two-ends approach to restriction for the truncated cone in $\R^n$, which gives the diagonal restriction range \[ p>2+\frac{4(7n+15)}{11n^2-n-24},\qquad n\ge10. \] This improves the range obtained by applying the result of Wang--Wu and then slicing.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyu Wang

item.title: Weighted Norm Inequalities for Maximal Multi-sublinear Rough Singular Integrals
item.description: arXiv:2610.18296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We continue our study of multilinear rough homogeneous singular integrals by establishing weighted estimates for their maximal truncations. Let $m\ge2$ and let $\Omega\in L^q(\mathbb{S}^{mn-1})$, $1<q\le\infty$, have mean zero. For $1<p_1,\dots,p_m<\infty$ with $p_j\ge q'$ and $1/p=\sum_{j=1}^m1/p_j$, we prove $$\big\Vert \mathcal{L}_\Omega^*(f_1,\dots,f_m)\big\Vert_{L^p(v_{\vec{\boldsymbol{w}}})} \lesssim \Vert\Omega\Vert_{L^q(\mathbb{S}^{mn-1})} \prod_{j=1}^m\Vert f_j\Vert_{L^{p_j}(w_j)}$$ whenever $\vec{\boldsymbol{w}}=(w_1,\dots,w_m)\in A_{(p_1/q',\dots,p_m/q')}$, where $q'$ is the H\"older conjugate of $q$ and $v_{\vec{\boldsymbol{w}}}=\prod_{j=1}^m w_j^{p/p_j}$. The estimate holds under the same multiple weight condition as the corresponding principal value estimate.
item.dc:creator: Bae Jun Park

item.title: Endpoint power weight inequalities for spherical maximal functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove sharp $L^p(|x|^\alpha)$ estimate for spherical maximal functions. We resolve the remaining open problem for the full maximal operator for $\alpha=1-d$ and $p<2$ and prove a more general result involving a local version of Assouad dimension of the underlying dilation set. We also make a case study with endpoint bounds for a model case involving convex sequences in $[1,2]$.
item.dc:creator: Marco Fraccaroli, Juyoung Lee, Nikou Lei, Joris Roos, Andreas Seeger

item.title: On the variation and asymptotics of maximal functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we present partial progress towards two conjectures on the variation of maximal operators of convolution type $\mathrm{M}_{\varphi}$, associated to non-negative and radial decreasing kernels $\varphi$ of integral $1$. In dimension $d=1$ we prove that $\mathrm{var}(\mathrm{M}_{\varphi} f) \leq \mathrm{var}(f)$ when $f$ is a characteristic function. In higher dimensions we prove that $\mathrm{var}(\mathrm{M}_{\varphi} f) \leq C_d \mathrm{var}(f)$ when $f$ is a radial characteristic function, with a constant $C_d$ depending only on the dimension $d$ but not on the kernel $\varphi$. We further show that $C_d \sim \sqrt{d}\log d $ is the sharp dependence on $d$ for such an inequality. This last claim relies on a novel explicit asymptotic estimate for the Hardy-Littlewood maximal function of the unit ball in $\mathbb R^d$, a result of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Emanuel Carneiro, Julian Weigt

item.title: Hypergeometric solutions to coupled Klein-Gordon equations in cosmology with small-field excursions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Klein-Gordon equation is a second order differential equation that appears in a variety of applications in mathematics, physics and engineering. This equation is often solved using numerical methods, since a general analytical solution is unattainable. However, one can find very useful analytical solutions for some special cases. In cosmology, the Klein-Gordon equation of a field can explain the physics of inflation and has important consequences on understanding the origin and evolution of the universe. An analytical solution to the Klein-Gordon equation in cosmology has been obtained in the small-field excursion approximation, and it turns out that the solution can be written in terms of the confluent hypergeometric limit function. In this work, we derive this result again while showing the details of the calculations and then generalize to the case of two coupled Klein-Gordon equations. We show that the solution of this coupled system can be written in terms of Kummer's hypergeometric limit function while considering minimal assumptions. We carry out a full numerical calculation of the coupled system and compare it to the results from the analytical expressions.
item.dc:creator: Amin Aboubrahim, Anastasiia Minenkova, Tomas Yonkers

item.title: Strong-type endpoint obstructions for bilinear spherical maximal operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.14201v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the bilinear spherical averages in dimension $d\geq2$, we show that the lacunary maximal operator is not bounded from $L^1(\mathbb R^d)\times L^q(\mathbb R^d)$ to $L^r(\mathbb R^d)$ whenever $1\leq q\leq\infty$ and $1/r=1+1/q$. The obstruction is realized by fixed nonnegative inputs; a second construction proves quantitative failure on smooth compactly supported functions and finitely many dyadic scales. The same conclusions hold for the full maximal operator. We give a sharp Lorentz-index criterion in the range $q>d/(d-1)$ and extend the negative result to all multilinear spherical maximal operators with an $L^1$ input. We indicate the precise strong-type boundary statements to which these conclusions apply, without drawing conclusions about separate weak-type or interior estimates.
item.dc:creator: Vicente Vergara

item.title: Asymptotically conical shrinking ends of the $r$-mean curvature flow: rotational construction and uniqueness
item.description: arXiv:2610.14227v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $1\leq r\leq n-1$ we study shrinking self-similar ends of the $r$-mean curvature flow, $S_r=c\langle X,N\rangle$ with $c<0$, that are asymptotic to a cone. For every rotational cone of positive slope we construct a smooth embedded rotational end and prove that its profile is the only positive solution of the profile equation with the prescribed slope at infinity. Its angular defect $xu'-u$ is strictly negative, which yields $r$-admissibility, and the profile has a complete asymptotic expansion for $u(x)/x$ in powers of $x^{-(r+1)}$, valid after arbitrary differentiation. The profiles depend real analytically on the slope and, on sufficiently distant exterior regions, foliate the image of the corresponding family. Our main result removes the symmetry assumption: two ends that converge smoothly, with multiplicity one, to the same circular cone coincide outside a compact set. The proof transforms the equation for their difference into an almost-eigenfunction inequality for a drift Laplacian on an auxiliary conical metric and applies Bernstein's asymptotic analysis on weakly conical ends. The argument extends to strictly $r$-admissible cones whose links have constant principal curvatures.
item.dc:creator: Hil\'ario Alencar, M\'arcio Batista, Greg\'orio Silva Neto

item.title: Sharp Constants and Extremizers in Homogeneous Tree BMO
item.description: arXiv:2610.14459v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a finite-tree formalism for sharp inequalities on real-valued, mean-centered $\operatorname{L}^1$-BMO over homogeneous $q$-ary filtrations. A reduction theorem identifies local and global sharp constants with the supremum of finite-depth constants. Finite anchoring gives compact optimization problems and rational extremizers under rational piecewise-linear hypotheses, while stable centering shows that imposing zero root average preserves the supremum over all depths. The principal application is the absolute-value map: we construct centered examples in which taking absolute values increases the BMO seminorm and obtain bounds strictly below the universal factor $2$. Jensen-defect Carleson functionals and martingale-difference envelopes provide further applications, illustrating distinct anchoring mechanisms and the differences between finite-depth rationality, stabilization, and global attainment.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadreza Mohajer

item.title: Cubic moments of eigenfunctions on surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16157v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We identify Gaussian curvature as a local mechanism for cubic cancellation of Laplace eigenfunctions on Riemannian surfaces, without arithmetic or dynamical assumptions. For $L^2$-normalized local solutions at frequency $\lambda$, cubic integrals against smooth compactly supported weights tend to zero whenever the curvature is nonzero almost everywhere where the weight is nonzero. Finite-order nondegeneracy yields sharp polynomial decay rates. In particular, on closed surfaces with nowhere-vanishing curvature, we obtain the rate $O(\lambda^{-1/6})$, attained by spherical harmonics on the round sphere. This proves the cubic case of the Gaussian moment conjecture for all normalized real eigenfunctions on closed negatively curved surfaces. The local proof rests on an exact identity relating the reduced phase at a Fermat point to Gaussian curvature. On complete hyperbolic surfaces with positive systole, we also prove global $O((\log\lambda)^{-3/2})$ decay for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions and smooth weights with bounded covariant derivatives through order two, without assuming finite area.
item.dc:creator: Xing Wang, Cheng Zhang

item.title: Contractivity of Rudin's diagonal restriction operator for $H^p$ of the polydisc
item.description: arXiv:2610.16227v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish that Rudin's diagonal restriction operator is contractive from the Hardy space $H^p$ of the bidisc to the Bergman space $A^p$ of the disc for $2\leq p<\infty$, and characterize all cases of equality. We extend the result to polydiscs and obtain applications to polynomial point evaluation among others. The proof relies on an explicit formula, deduced from certain Green's formulas, for the defect between the $p$th powers of the two $L^p$ norms.
item.dc:creator: Ole Fredrik Brevig, Javier G\'omez-Serrano, Joaquim Ortega-Cerd\`{a}, Kristian Seip

item.title: Vanishing Events and Regularity-Conditioned Reachability in Linear Stieltjes Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.17345v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study linear Stieltjes control systems in which actuation is concentrated at finitely many temporal events, and we ask what happens when one of those events progressively loses its atomic weight in the associated Stieltjes measure. For constant coefficients, ordinary finite-atomic reachability is governed by a truncated Krylov space and is therefore insensitive to the positive values of the event weights. A different picture emerges once trajectory regularity is imposed. In the supercritical super-$g$-H\"older regime, we minimize the largest event-normalized state jump and characterize exactly the terminal directions for which this cost remains uniformly bounded as a prescribed event weight tends to zero. The characterization combines what can be reached before the vulnerable event, a drift-cancellability condition at that event, and the directions that remain available afterwards. Ordinary reachability of the deleted-event system can therefore be strictly larger than bounded-cost reachability in the singular limit. We also separate two mechanisms of divergence: loss of ordinary reachability after deletion and failure of the intermediate compatibility condition. For compatible targets, the minimum cost converges to a constrained deleted-event problem. A dimensionless position--velocity benchmark motivated by pulsed proximity maneuvers shows the distinction explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Francisco J. Fern\'andez

item.title: Coding multiplicity in self-similar sets on the line
item.description: arXiv:2610.18392v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study coding multiplicity for self-similar sets on the real line. When the similarity dimension exceeds one, almost every point with respect to the natural self-similar measure has infinitely many codings. We focus on the case when the similarity dimension is at most one. Our analysis proceeds through the recurrence properties and the size of the critical set, defined as the union of the pairwise intersections of the first-level pieces. Our main structural result shows that when the critical set is finite, unboundedness of coding multiplicity is equivalent to periodic recurrence to the critical set. Moreover, every commensurable system with a finite critical set has uniformly bounded coding multiplicity. This conclusion is sharp in the incommensurable setting. We construct a one-parameter family of four-map systems such that for Lebesgue almost every parameter, the critical set is a singleton and the open set condition fails, while the attractor contains a point with infinitely many codings. More generally, for transversal families, the set of parameters admitting an infinite coding fibre is dense among those for which the strong separation condition fails. We also obtain a quantitative lower bound for the Hausdorff dimension of this parameter set. Such parameters can form a meagre set. We continue the study of the geometric size of branching, obtaining dimension formulae for typical coding fibres and almost-sure upper bounds on the dimension of the critical set in transversal families. In contrast, we construct an exponentially separated system with no dimension drop whose critical set has the same Hausdorff dimension as the attractor and whose coding map has a fibre of continuum cardinality. Although we work in the one-dimensional setting, several results and arguments extend to higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: K\'aroly Simon, Jian-Ci Xiao

item.title: A proof of Saari's homographic conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2212.10148v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove Saari's homographic conjecture for a large class of $n$-body problems with power law potentials, including the classical $n$-body problem.
item.dc:creator: Pieter Tibboel

item.title: On Type IV Superorthogonality
item.description: arXiv:2312.01717v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the direct and the converse inequality for type IV superorthogonality in the vector-valued setting. The converse one is also new in the scalar setting.
item.dc:creator: Jianghao Zhang

item.title: Sharp restriction estimates for some degenerate higher codimensional quadratic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2404.09020v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Fourier restriction conjecture is a fundamental problem in harmonic analysis. In this paper, we investigate restriction estimates for degenerate higher codimensional quadratic surfaces and obtain sharp results for some types of degenerate cases. A major obstacle in establishing sharp restriction estimates is the failure of rescaling invariance, which is crucial for induction on scale to be effective. Motivated by the work of Guo and Oh (2022), we introduce a method, building on an iterative variant of the broad-narrow analysis, that does not heavily rely on induction on scale. To obtain suitable transversality conditions for this analysis and to derive desirable bounds for the broad part, we define a generalized notion of Jacobian, and establish its structural properties. These properties are proved using tools and techniques from both algebra and graph theory.
item.dc:creator: Zhenbin Cao, Changxing Miao, Yixuan Pang

item.title: Asymptotics of matrix orthogonal polynomials on the real line
item.description: arXiv:2508.04908v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we are interested in matrix valued orthogonal polynomials on the real line with respect to exponential weights. We obtain strong asymptotics as the degree tends to infinity in different regions of the complex plane, as well as asymptotic behavior of recurrence coefficients and norms. The main tools are the Riemann-Hilbert formulation and the Deift-Zhou method of steepest descent, adapted to the matrix case. A central role is played by the matrix Szeg\H{o} function, an object that has independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Alfredo Dea\~no, Pablo Rom\'an

item.title: Quantitative homogenization of first-order ODEs
item.description: arXiv:2508.17628v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates the quantitative homogenization of first-order ODEs. For single-scale scalar ODEs, we obtain a sharp $O(\varepsilon)$ convergence rate and characterize the effective constant. In the multi-scale setting, our results match those of \cite{IM} for long times but improve the short-time error to $O(\varepsilon)$. We also obtain what appears to be the first uniform $O(\varepsilon)$ homogenization estimate for scalar ODEs with quasi-periodic fast dependence on the state variable. The scalar framework is further extended to higher dimensions under a bounded-mean-motion-type assumption. For weakly coupled systems with fast switching rates, we derive an explicit $O(\varepsilon)$ convergence rate that captures the initial layer. These results have applications to linear transport equations and broader connections to PDEs and gradient systems.
item.dc:creator: Panrui Ni

item.title: The p-spectrum of Random Wavelet Series
item.description: arXiv:2510.00622v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The goal of multifractal analysis is to characterize variations in local regularity of functions by computing the Hausdorff dimension of sets of points sharing the same regularity. While classical approaches rely on H\"older exponents and are restricted to locally bounded functions, $p$-exponents extend this framework to functions locally in $L^p$ and allow one to describe negative regularities. We establish a wavelet-based upper bound for the $p$-spectrum in terms of the asymptotic distribution of wavelet coefficients, extending the classical H\"older case. We then compute the exact $p$-spectrum of \textit{Random Wavelet Series} and show that, for non-negative regularities, this bound is sharp and is also attained by a prevalent set of functions with a prescribed wavelet statistic. Finally, we show that a different phenomenon occurs for negative regularities: contrary to the classical H\"older case, Random Wavelet Series do not in general realize the maximal $p$-spectrum compatible with a prescribed distribution of wavelet coefficients.
item.dc:creator: C\'eline Esser, Thelma Lambert, B\'eatrice Vedel

item.title: On Constructions of full-dimensional absolutely normal sets of uniqueness
item.description: arXiv:2601.03402v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct a class of homogeneous Cantor-Moran measures with all contraction ratios being reciprocals of integers, and prove that they are pointwise absolutely normal. Our approach relies on methods developed by Davenport, Erd{\H{o}}s and LeVeque and properties of the order of integers in the multiplicative groups. The construction of these measures differs from the class of pointwise absolutely normal self-similar measures introduced by Hochman and Shmerkin, in which dynamical approaches were used. As an application, for all gauge functions $\varphi(r)$ with $r/\varphi(r)\to 0$ as $r\to 0$, we obtain a set of uniqueness $K$ with ${\mathcal H}^{\varphi}(K)>0$. Moreover, we show that there exists a pointwise absolutely normal measure $ \mu $ of dimension one fully supported on $ K $. The result shows that the simultaneous $\mathsf{DEL}$ control in every integer base can occur on a support that carries no nonzero Rajchman measure. Thus, the usual Fourier-decay mechanism for proving normality is sufficient but is far from necessary.
item.dc:creator: Chun-Kit Lai, Yu-Hao Xie

item.title: A streamlined proof of the Kakeya set conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^3$
item.description: arXiv:2601.14411v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a streamlined and simplified proof of the Kakeya set conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^3$.
item.dc:creator: Larry Guth, Hong Wang, Joshua Zahl

item.title: Maximal growth of the Stein-Wainger oscillatory integral
item.description: arXiv:2603.23238v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the optimal growth of the Stein--Wainger oscillatory integral for every Denjoy--Carleman class defined by a positive log-convex sequence. Quasianalyticity is equivalent to boundedness in $\lambda$ for every fixed phase in the class. In the nonquasianalytic case, an explicit formula in the defining sequence gives the optimal order, attained by a single phase for all sufficiently large frequencies. This yields sharp bounds for Gevrey classes, their logarithmic refinements, and classes beyond every Gevrey class. For general smooth phases the growth is $o(\log\lambda)$, and every prescribed $h(\lambda)\to\infty$ with $h(\lambda)=o(\log\lambda)$ is attained asymptotically along a sequence by one smooth phase. These results answer a question of Wang and Zhang motivated by endpoint eigenfunction restriction.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Zhang, Zhifei Zhu

item.title: A discussion of two arguments related to Fefferman's Fourier extension theorem in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2605.20100v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Fourier extension conjecture of E. Stein was proved in the plane in 1970 by C. Fefferman, see also Zygmund and Carleson and Sj\"olin, with simplifications given by other authors later on, in particular by L. H\"ormander and T. Tao. We discuss yet two more arguments for this classical theorem on the parabola. The first argument uses C. Fefferman's decoupling together with a decomposition into Haar wavelets. This sets the stage for the second argument whose point of departure is the bilinear characterization of Tao, Vargas and Vega, and relies on the bilinear interplay with the classical wave packet constructions and discrete characterizations with an induction on scales. Each of the above two arguments rely on some form of Fefferman's convolution decoupling and the special nature of the critical planar index 4 as a positive even integer, but the second might be more amenable to weighted generalizations.
item.dc:creator: Eric T. Sawyer

item.title: Fourier analytic variants of the Furstenberg and Kakeya problems
item.description: arXiv:2605.21668v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study several distinct but related Fourier analytic variants of the well-known Kakeya and Furstenberg set problems in the plane. For example, given $0<s,t<1$, we call a set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ an $(s,t)$-Kakeya set if there exists a set of directions $E \subseteq S^1$ with Hausdorff dimension at least $t$ such that, for each $e \in E$, the set $K$ contains a subset of a unit line segment in direction $e$ whose Fourier dimension, viewed as a subset of $\mathbb{R}$, is at least $s$. For $\Delta(s,t)$ defined to be the infimum of the Fourier dimension among all $(s,t)$-Kakeya sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$, we prove that \[ \Delta(s,t) = \min\{s,2t\}. \] We also obtain similar results in the Furstenberg set version of the problem and in the case where the Hausdorff dimension of the collection of lines is replaced by the Fourier dimension.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan M. Fraser, Lijian Yang

item.title: Hardy space estimates for the parabolic maximal operator below $p=1$
item.description: arXiv:2607.15427v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the parabolic maximal operator $M_{\textrm{par}}$ along the moment curve $(t,t^2)$. In 1988, Christ proved that $M_{\textrm{par}}$ maps the parabolic Hardy space $H_{\textrm{par}}^1(\mathbb R^2)$ into $L^{1,\infty}(\mathbb R^2)$. We show that this result is sharp at $p=1$: for every $0<p<1$, the natural extension from $H_{\textrm{par}}^p(\mathbb R^2)$ to $L^{p,\infty}(\mathbb R^2)$ fails even for the corresponding single-scale operator. We then introduce a curvature-adapted modified Hardy space $H_{\textrm{par}}^{p,*}(\mathbb R^2)$ and a weak tendril space $\mathcal T^{p,\infty}(\mathbb R^2)$, and prove that $$ M_{\textrm{par}}: H_{\textrm{par}}^{p,*}(\mathbb R^2) \longrightarrow \mathcal T^{p,\infty}(\mathbb R^2), \qquad 0<p<1, $$ is bounded. At $p=1$, these spaces recover those in Christ's theorem: $H_{\textrm{par}}^{1,*}(\mathbb R^2)=H_{\textrm{par}}^1(\mathbb R^2)$ and $\mathcal T^{1,\infty}(\mathbb R^2)=L^{1,\infty}(\mathbb R^2)$. Thus, our result provides a natural extension of Christ's work to the range $0<p<1$.
item.dc:creator: Yongsheng Han, Bingyang Hu

item.title: Tur\'an problem on the union of three intervals of equal length
item.description: arXiv:2608.15643v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper addresses the Tur\'an extremal problem on the symmetric three-interval set $\Omega_\lambda = (-1,1) \cup (\lambda-1,\lambda+1) \cup (-\lambda-1,-\lambda+1)$, $\lambda \geq 0$. We establish a discrete approximation principle relating the continuous Tur\'an problem on $\Omega_\lambda$ to the discrete Tur\'an problem on an associated finite discrete set. This enables the continuous problem to be exactly expressed as a limit of finite nonnegative trigonometric polynomial problems, which are equivalent to finite semidefinite programs. Using this framework, we compute the Tur\'an constant for integer and rational parameters $\lambda$. We further analyze the dependence of the Tur\'an constant on $\lambda$ and derive upper bounds for all $\lambda > 5$.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Ye Fu, Yue-Kun Li, Wei-Jie Wang, Xuan Wang

item.title: On the matrix $A_p$ conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.14584v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper provides a solution to the matrix $A_p$ conjecture. For every \(1<p<\infty\), we construct a family of \(2\times2\) matrix \(A_p\) weights $W$ with arbitrarily large characteristics for which \[\|H\|_{L^p(W)\to L^p(W)}\ge c_p[W]_{A_p}^{1+1/[p(p-1)]},\] where \(H\) is the Hilbert transform and \(c_p>0\) depends only on \(p\).
item.dc:creator: Yong Jiao, Xingyan Quan, Lian Wu, Guangheng Xie

item.title: On the Central Maximal Function in $\mathbb{R}^n$
item.description: arXiv:2609.27687v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the central Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator in $\mathbb{R}^n$. For every integer $n\geq1$, we construct two bounded, nonnegative functions $f,g\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$ that differ on a set of positive measure and satisfy $M_cf(x)=M_cg(x)$ at every point $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Thus the central maximal operator is not injective on the nonnegative cone of $L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$. The functions can have compact support; when $n\geq2$, they can also be chosen radial, either with compact support or strictly positive throughout the space. The construction makes a small redistribution of mass invisible to the maximal operator by excluding averaging spheres that cross its support. We also give an explicit formula, in terms of the incomplete beta function, for the $n$-dimensional volume of the intersection of two balls with arbitrary radii and centers, and an elementary formula for the central maximal function of a ball in $\mathbb{R}^3$.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Solyanik

item.title: A Formalism for Merging Power Series in Solving Multinomial Equations: Master Series and Master Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2609.33459v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is shown that all solutions of the canonical equation y^a = 1 + a*x*y^b with arbitrary complex exponents a, b (case m = 1) and of its limiting cases - the binomial root y = (1 + a*x)^(1/a) at b = 0, the exponential y = e^x at a = 0, b = 0, and the Lambert equation y = e^(x*y^b) at a = 0 - as well as the logarithms of these solutions (case m = 0), are expressed by a single power master series M(m; a; b; x) = m + x + ((m - a + 2b)/2!) x^2 + ((m - a + 3b)(m - 2a + 3b)/3!) x^3 + ... For multivalued solutions beyond the radius of convergence, a geometric criterion for selecting the conjugate series (the same master series, but with a different set of parameters M(m; a'; b'; x')) is proposed, ensuring branch continuity on the complex plane. This representation of power series in terms of master numbers not only allows one to compute coefficients in degenerate cases where the gamma-function representation loses meaning, but also provides a transparent analytical algorithm for the merge operation on master series. The method is illustrated on problems in gas dynamics and plasma physics, where it is demonstrated that physically realizable states require the application of conjugate series beyond the radius of convergence of the basic expansion.
item.dc:creator: Sergey V. Berezin

item.title: Sharp Matrix-Weighted Lower Bounds for Non-Degenerate Convolution Calder\'on--Zygmund Operators
item.description: arXiv:2609.33560v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $T$ be a convolution Calder\'on--Zygmund operator satisfying Hyt\"onen's non-degeneracy condition. We prove that, for every $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $m\ge3$, there exists a positive constant $C$ such that, for any $t\in[1,\infty)$, \begin{equation*} \sup_{[W]_{\mathcal A_p}\le t} \|T\|_{L^p(W)\to L^p(W)} \ge C t^{1+\frac{1}{p(p-1)}}, \end{equation*} where the supremum is taken over all matrix weights $W:\ \mathbb R^n\to\mathbb C^{m\times m}$ with their weight constants $[W]_{\mathcal A_p}\le t$. If, in addition, the odd part of the kernel is non-degenerate (such as the Hilbert transform and the Riesz transforms), the same conclusion holds for every $m\ge2$.
item.dc:creator: Fan Bu, Dachun Yang, Wen Yuan

item.title: Weak type $(1,1)$ bounds for oscillatory singular integrals with rough kernels
item.description: arXiv:2610.02789v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In their seminal work, F. Ricci and E. M. Stein [Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. USA 83, 1--3 (1986)] introduced the oscillatory singular integral \[ T_Pf(x)=\mathrm{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} e^{iP(x,y)}\frac{\Omega(x-y)}{|x-y|^n}f(y)\,dy, \] and S. Chanillo and M. Christ [Duke Math. J. 55, 141--155 (1987)] established its weak-type $(1,1)$ inequality for smooth $\Omega$. For the rough variant, however, the weak-type $(1,1)$ inequality remained a long-standing open question. In the present paper, we settle this problem: specifically, we prove that the rough oscillatory singular integral is of weak type $(1,1)$ with $\Omega\in L\log^+L(\mathbb{S}^{n-1})$. Moreover, we establish weak-type $(1,1)$ bounds for the rough maximal oscillatory operator associated with $T_P$, a result of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Yanping Chen, Zhengyang Ji

item.title: Testing compactness of linear operators
item.description: arXiv:2411.17654v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $(F_i)$ be a sequence of sets in a Banach space $X$. For what sequences does the condition $$ \lim_{i\to \infty} \sup_{f_i\in F_i} \|Tf_i\|_Y=0 $$ hold for every Banach space $Y$ and every compact operator $T:X\to Y$? We answer this question by giving sufficient (and necessary) criteria for such sequences. We illustrate the applicability of the criteria by examples from the literature and by characterizing the $L^p\to L^p$ compactness of dyadic paraproducts on general measure spaces through introducing a space of vanishing mean oscillations with respect to mass (as opposed to length) of cubes.
item.dc:creator: Timo S. H\"anninen, Tuomas Oikari

item.title: On exponential separation of analytic self-conformal sets on the real line
item.description: arXiv:2509.07888v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In a recent article, Rapaport showed that there is no dimension drop for exponentially separated analytic IFSs on the real line. We show that the set of such exponentially separated IFSs in the space of analytic IFSs contains an open and dense set in the $\mathcal{C}^2$ topology. Moreover, we give a sufficient condition for the IFS to be exponentially separated which allows us to construct explicit examples which are exponentially separated. The key technical tool is the introduction of the \emph{dual IFS} which we believe has significant interest in its own right. As an application we also characterise when an analytic IFS can be conjugated to a self-similar IFS.
item.dc:creator: Bal\'azs B\'ar\'any, Istv\'an Kolossv\'ary, Sascha Troscheit

item.title: Combinatorial Bounds for List Recovery via Discrete Brascamp--Lieb Inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2510.13775v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In coding theory, the problem of list recovery asks one to find all codewords $c$ of a given code $C$ which such that at least $1-\rho$ fraction of the symbols of $c$ lie in some predetermined set of $\ell$ symbols for each coordinate of the code. A key question is bounding the maximum possible list size $L$ of such codewords for the given code $C$. In this paper, we give novel combinatorial bounds on the list recoverability of various families of linear and folded linear codes, including random linear codes, random Reed--Solomon codes, explicit folded Reed--Solomon codes, and explicit univariate multiplicity codes. Our main result is that in all of these settings, we show that for code of rate $R$, when $\rho = 1 - R - \epsilon$ approaches capacity, the list size $L$ is at most $(\ell/(R+\epsilon))^{O(R/\epsilon)}$. These results also apply in the average-radius regime. Our result resolves a long-standing open question on whether $L$ can be bounded by a polynomial in $\ell$. In the zero-error regime, our bound on $L$ perfectly matches known lower bounds. The primary technique is a novel application of a discrete entropic Brascamp--Lieb inequality to the problem of list recovery, allowing us to relate the local structure of each coordinate with the global structure of the recovered list. As a result of independent interest, we show that a recent result by Chen and Zhang (STOC 2025) on the list decodability of folded Reed--Solomon codes can be generalized into a novel Brascamp--Lieb type inequality.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Brakensiek, Yeyuan Chen, Manik Dhar, Zihan Zhang

item.title: On Singular Integrals and Quantitative Rectifiability in Parabolic Space and the Heisenberg Group
item.description: arXiv:2510.26934v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: David and Semmes proved that if all CZOs (of suitable dimension) are bounded with respect to an Ahlfors regular measure, then the measure is uniformly rectifiable. We extend this theorem to the parabolic space and to all Heisenberg groups.
item.dc:creator: John Hoffman, Benjamin Jaye

item.title: Pointwise character bounds for $\mathrm{SU}(3)$
item.description: arXiv:2604.17589v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a basic pointwise bound for the irreducible characters of $\mathrm{SU}(3)$ and, as an application, derive new $L^p$ bounds for these characters. Our approach is based on the descent of characters to singular sets and the cancellation in this formula.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. 58 (2026), no. 10, Paper No. e70519, 24 pp
item.dc:creator: Yunfeng Zhang

item.title: Optimal Extrapolation Bounds for Sparse Fourier Sums
item.dc:creator: Ruizhe Zhang

item.title: Range Failure, Resolvent Growth, and Resonance in Partially Dissipative Systems
item.description: arXiv:2609.17712v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce several notions of resonance for systems exhibiting weak or partial dissipation: $\dot u=Au+f(t)$, with $A$ the generator of a strongly stable semigroup $S(t)$ on a Hilbert space $H$. We refer to resonance as the phenomenon where a time-periodic $f$ may yield an unbounded $u$, classically occurring when $A$ has imaginary eigenvalues. In infinite dimensions, however, unbounded growth may depend on topological choices, and several ``resonances" may occur. Classically, existence of $T$-periodic $u$ under $T$-periodic $f$ is equivalent to a range condition: $\mathcal{R}(I-S(T))=H$. Consequently, its failure permits unbounded solution growth and we elucidate that connection through properties of $S(t)$. We describe a hierarchy of range failures, and provide an associated resonance taxonomy. The growth rate of ~$||(A-\lambda I)^{-1}||_H$ on ~$i\R$ dictates a regularity gap between $u$ and $f$, and, for rapid growth in $\lambda$, that gap can be infinite. In this case, we demonstrate implications for periodic solvability, and a mechanism for constructing smooth resonant forces. The theory developed here is motivated by (and demonstrated for) a hyperbolic-parabolic system, where the latter component provides the only system dissipation. Such dynamics are a simplification of fluid-structure phenomena, which demonstrate strong stability but do not provide unconditional periodic well-posedness. Though point-spectral resonance is ruled out, we note that $\mathcal R(I-S(T))\neq H$. Our main result here shows that, for a carefully constructed geometry, a classical heat-wave system possesses periods $T$ which yield infinite derivative loss and, via supporting results, yield resonance with smooth forcing.

item.title: Fourier Ratio and Restricted Isometry via Entropic Descent
item.description: arXiv:2609.22568v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this second paper on descent methods as proof mechanisms in harmonic analysis (the first treated Bourgain's $\Lambda(p)$ selection theorem), entropic mirror descent gives an improved restricted isometry bound, improving sampling and recovery bounds in the Fourier Ratio program. Let $H$ be a complex $n\times n$ matrix with $H^*H=nI$ and $|H_{ij}|=1$. For fixed $0<\varepsilon<\frac14$ and $A_0>0$, independent Bernoulli row selection with expected cardinality $C_{\varepsilon,A_0}r\log\frac{2en}{r}\log(2r)\leq m\leq n/2$ preserves, after normalization by $\sqrt m$, the squared norm of every complex vector $y$ with $\|y\|_1\leq\sqrt r\|y\|_2$ within a factor $1\pm\varepsilon$, with failure probability at most $Cn^{-A_0}$. This includes every $r$-sparse vector and also fully supported ones; support size enters only through this inequality. For $y=\widehat f$ the condition is exactly $\operatorname{FR}(f)^2\leq r$, where $\operatorname{FR}(f)=\|\widehat f\|_1/\|\widehat f\|_2$, giving uniform energy sampling and approximate recovery even for signals with full Fourier support. The same holds for a uniform subset of prescribed cardinality, and for discrete Fourier and real Hadamard matrices. At fixed accuracy the bound removes one sparsity logarithm from the earlier count and replaces $\log n$ by $\log\frac{2en}{r}$; for Walsh matrices it matches, up to constants, the lower bound of B\l asiok et al.\ in their range. One relative-entropy potential controls the corrections of an amplitude predictor at every scale; counting them on the symmetric difference of two samples gives the uniform estimate. We also prove the sufficient bound $C_{A_0}\varepsilon^{-5}r\log\frac{2en}{r}\log\frac{2r}{\varepsilon}$, and stable sparse recovery from $Cs\log\frac{2en}{s}\log(2s)$ measurements, with error controlled by the noise and the best $s$-term approximation.
item.dc:creator: W. Burstein, A. Iosevich, B. Krause

item.title: A geometric rigidity estimate for codimension-1 immersions into spheres
item.description: arXiv:2609.37665v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a quantitative stability estimate for codimension-one immersions into a round sphere. Let $(M,g)$ be an oriented Riemannian manifold and suppose that a prescribed shape operator is realised by a smooth isometric immersion $\theta:(M,g)\to\mathbb S^{n+1}$. We prove that, on every relatively compact strongly Lipschitz domain and for every $1<p<\infty$, any Sobolev immersion $\phi$ is close to $\theta$ modulo an ambient rotation, with the $W^{1,p}$-distances between both the immersions and their Gauss maps controlled by the $L^p$ stretching-plus-bending energies of $\phi$. No {\it a priori} bounds on the fundamental forms of $\phi$ are required. The proof proceeds by extending the immersions along normal geodesics and reducing the problem to an equidimensional geometric rigidity estimate on the sphere. A finite localisation and patching argument handles the possible non-injectivity of the normal extension of the reference immersion.
item.dc:creator: Siran Li, Isaac Newell
